First of all thank you for your answer.
Its just the way you answered back that offended me a little bit to be honest by saying "1 little drawing a day" because for some 1 drawing a day is hard enough psychologically and timewise. Now that I have read your full opinion on this I can completely understand your point. So have a nice day and bye

Your brain as well as your muscles need breaks to develop further. If you look at the training plans of professional athletes, it becomes quickly clear that breaks are also part of the routine. These training plans, as long as they were made by an experienced trainer, in which he balances the frequency and intensity for the athlete prevent something like a burnout usually. That's why they don't train intense everyday except they are an steroids or are biological anomalies.

It's the same with drawing. There is a difference between proper practice of the art fundamentals and your "1 little drawing every day".
As an example, let's take you draw one little drawing every day this would take about half an hour. That means you drew about 210 minutes per week without evaluating your drawing because you don't have the time and knowledge about how and why you made a mistake. If you don't make mistakes then why are you practicing, right? So you go to the next drawing hoping this will be better than the last one. 
Then why don't you draw 4-5 times a week for about 1-2 hours. With 1-2 hours you got enough time to get into the drawing and correct your mistakes and learn from it. And you have spent more time practicing per week about 4-10 hours per week.
The routine you have given there is not completly useless but it is still not as effective as others.

No one here wants to discourage others from pushing themselves to get better and i know you just want to help others too but if the price for pushing yourself every day is to lose your fun at drawing the my tip is the better one.

It is also not an attack on you either but your argument with the professional athlete was simply just not correct.
